etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French desplacer (French: déplacer).

definitions.definition: To put out of place; to disarrange.
To move something, or someone, especially to forcibly move people from their homeland.

quote.citation: 2023 May 8, “Manipur: Thousands displaced as ethnic clashes grip north-eastern state”, in BBC News‎[1]:
quote.text: Manipur: Thousands displaced as ethnic clashes grip north-eastern state

definitions.definition: To supplant, or take the place of something or someone; to substitute.
To replace, on account of being superior to or more suitable than that which is being replaced.

quote.citation: 1950 January, Cecil J. Allen, “British Locomotive Practice and Performance”, in Railway Magazine, page 13:
quote.text: All have gone the same way, and since the war have displaced up-to-date steam power on all their principal services by the all-conquering diesel.

definitions.definition: (of a floating ship) To have a weight equal to that of the water displaced.

quote.citation: 2017, Megan Garber, “The Case for Shyness”, in The Atlantic‎[2]:
quote.text: Freud considered shyness to be evidence of displaced narcissism.
